M2 is the corrupted element. Its width is 2.892 µm, while M1 is 20.23 µm with the same L. That gives a mirror ratio of 0.143 (about 1/7) instead of 1. The simulated output of 2.748 µA is about 0.137 × 20 µA, which matches the 86% error. The input node at 0.67 V is consistent with M1 carrying 20 µA at its drawn width, so M1 looks intact. Output resistance and compliance pass because they don't depend on the ratio.
